I am farming sorghum on my 1.36 hectare plot here in the North West. The rains are our life — we have no irrigation, so I plant when the sky tells me. I will buy some urea and NPK from the market if the price is fair, and I spread the manure from my goats and cattle before planting. I keep my own sorghum seed from last harvest because the local variety does well with our short rains, and I intercrop with cowpea as we always do. My two sons help me, but at weeding time I must hire some young men from the village because the weeds come fast.
